title: Headlamp at first light
suits: agriculture, forestry, supply-chain traceability, land and climate data, field-work and rural products; any pitch whose day starts before dawn

params.--field: the sky by day (indigo by default; any colour or gradient), shaded to pre-dawn so the name always reads
params.--brand: tints the name's cream ink (12%), so a dark brand still reads light
params.--brand-2: tints the first light behind the ridge and the land
params.--hl-fs: name size (212 px); long names shrink so mark and name fit 1640 px
params.__MARK__: stroke paths with pathLength="1" in a 24 x 24 box, drawn on one after another

details: the near worker's headlamp clicks on with a stutter (on, off, on in 90 ms), like a cheap switch
the beam starts on the fresh tapping cut of the tree beside them before it swings up
the beam finds the letters one by one, still blurred in the mist, before the mist lifts off them
first light rises behind the karst while the beam sweeps, and the stars fade with it, the morning star last
the headlamp clicks off the same way at 2 s, because it is light enough now
the mark draws itself stroke after stroke, after the name is clear
far workers' headlamps stop at each tree for a few seconds, their faint cone on the trunk, then walk to the next; at the row's end they turn and work back
each far headlamp bobs slightly with the worker's step
a satellite crosses the sky as a steady, unblinking moving point, once every 47 s
near trees carry a real tapping panel: faint healed cuts below, renewed bark, the fresh ochre cut at about 25 degrees with latex along it, a spout and a cup on a wire
about every nine seconds one drop of latex gathers at a spout and falls into the cup, each tree out of step
the karst towers are spires, sheer blocks and domes with a ragged forest fringe along their tops
a low mist lies at the feet of the karst and drifts slowly
the plot floor is littered with orange-red leaves
print and reduced motion show the finished lockup at first light, with no blur or blended layers
